meta.title: About Metal Form — manufacturing since 2006
meta.description: A mould-making workshop that grew into an engineering, tooling, manufacturing and supply business. Since 2006, more than a thousand completed projects. One accountable partner for the whole route.

headline: Since 2006
of cutting steel
for other people’s parts.
hero.lead: Metal Form has designed and built moulds and supplied moulded components since 2006. Today we coordinate engineering, tooling, production and supply under one project, with one technical contact accountable for the result.

sections.title: What we actually are
body: A tooling business first. Injection moulds, PET and closure tooling, blow and die-cast work, multi-cavity tools, hot and cold runner systems, insert tooling and the mechanisms that make awkward geometry possible. More than a thousand projects have gone through the workshop since 2006.

Around that foundation the company now takes on the parts of a project that sit either side of the tool: the engineering that decides whether a part can be made economically at all, and the production and supply that follow once it can.
For a customer that means one contract, one technical contact and one party answerable for the outcome — whether the work is a single tool or a component supplied every month for years.

sections.title: How the work is organised
body: Metal Form coordinates the route. Engineering, tool manufacture, production and supply are managed as one project against one specification, and the responsibility for the result does not move between parties when something goes wrong.

Coordinating the stages under one project reduces handover gaps between design, tooling and production. That is the commercial point: fewer interfaces to manage and clearer responsibility when a change is needed.
Engineering and tool manufacture are coordinated closely, so questions about geometry, steel and production can be resolved without long handovers.

sections.title: How cross-sector tooling experience helps
body: Working across different tooling sectors exposes the same core decisions in different forms: flow, cooling, wear, mechanisms, repeatability and maintenance. That cross-over is useful when a new part does not fit a familiar template.

That breadth is unusual and it is genuinely useful. A dripper tool teaches you things about high cavitation that a heavy-vehicle bracket never will; a cosmetic closure teaches you things about show surfaces that a fitting never will. Both turn up again in the next project.
Country of origin, shipping route and delivery terms are stated in the commercial documents for each project rather than used as a substitute for technical proof.

sections.title: Where we are going
body: The intention is to keep growing the engineering and supply side of the business rather than only the workshop: more engineering capacity, more production routes, more capability to take responsibility for a component from concept through to a rolling delivery schedule.
That is an intention, not a capability. Everything else on this site describes what Metal Form can do today.

accountability.heading: One partner remains accountable from start to finish.
body: Metal Form coordinates engineering, tooling, machining, production and supply as one project. The exact manufacturing route is defined for each job; the customer keeps one Metal Form technical contact.

Design decisions are reviewed with tooling and production in view. Corrections, spares and changes are managed against the same project specification so responsibility does not have to move between suppliers.
